chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Hajj is in the well-known months: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijja. It is not for anyone to perform Hajj in what is besides these.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific months for performing Hajj in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific temporal boundaries for the Hajj pilgrimage, identifying Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijja as the 'well-known months' (Ashhur Ma'lumat). It establishes the legal ruling that the obligatory Hajj is strictly confined to these months, distinguishing them from other times when only Umrah or voluntary acts may be performed. This specification aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding of the sanctity of these months as periods of divine decree for pilgrimage.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Musna Al Hannat, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
[2:197] The Hajj is (performed in) the well-known months – Shawwal, and Zil-Qadah, and Zil-Hijja. It is not for anyone that he performs Hajj in what is besides these’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Muthanna’ al- Hannat from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The months of al-Hajj are well known’ [2:197]; they are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa’dah and Dhu al-Hajj ah. No one has the right to perform al-Hajj in months other than these ones.’”
